questions.question: In Y = β₀ + β₁X₁ + β₂X₂ + ε, what does β₁ represent in the fitted model?
options: The change in fitted Y per unit of X₁, holding X₂ fixed
The effect of X₁ on its own, ignoring all other columns
The correlation between X₁ and X₂
questions.explanation: A multiple-regression coefficient describes a conditional fitted change while the other included predictors are held fixed.

questions.question: Using X̃ for a design matrix that includes an intercept column, which is the OLS closed-form solution when X̃ᵀX̃ is invertible?
questions.explanation: Differentiating the squared-error objective gives X̃ᵀX̃β̂ = X̃ᵀy; invertibility yields the stated solution.

questions.question: Perfect collinearity between two design-matrix columns causes:
options: A unique coefficient estimate with smaller variance
X̃ᵀX̃ to be singular, so the coefficient vector is not uniquely identified by the normal equations
The model to stop using least squares
questions.explanation: A nonzero vector v can satisfy X̃v = 0, so multiple coefficient vectors can produce the same fitted values.

questions.question: A large variance inflation factor (VIF) most directly signals that:
options: A predictor is strongly explained by other predictors, inflating its coefficient variance
The model needs more training iterations
questions.explanation: VIFⱼ = 1/(1 − Rⱼ²), where Rⱼ² comes from regressing feature j on the other features. It is a multicollinearity diagnostic, not a causal measure.

questions.question: On the same training rows, what happens to ordinary least-squares training R² when a predictor is added to a nested model?
options: It cannot decrease, though it may stay unchanged
questions.explanation: The larger nested model can set the added coefficient to zero, so its minimum training SSE cannot be worse; this does not guarantee better test performance.

questions.question: Adjusted R² differs from R² mainly because it:
options: Uses absolute error instead of squared error
Accounts for the number of predictors and penalises unnecessary additions
Always increases when a feature is added
questions.explanation: Adjusted R² accounts for sample size and predictor count, so it can decrease when an added feature contributes too little.

questions.question: Which is a reasonable response to severe multicollinearity when prediction is the goal?
options: Add still more copies of the same information
Consider removing a redundant feature or using a regularised model such as Ridge
Use test data to choose the coefficient signs
questions.explanation: Removing redundant predictors or using regularisation can improve stability; interpret the choice in light of the task.

questions.question: There are n = 100 rows and p = 3 predictors. If X̃ includes an intercept column, what is its shape?
questions.explanation: The augmented matrix has one column per predictor plus one leading column of ones for the intercept.

questions.question: For independent errors with common variance σ² and a full-rank augmented design X̃, what is Var(β̂OLS)?
options: The identity matrix for every dataset
questions.explanation: Under the stated error assumptions, Var(β̂OLS) = σ²(X̃ᵀX̃)⁻¹.

questions.question: Adding a correlated predictor can change the sign of an existing multiple-regression coefficient.
questions.explanation: Correlated predictors share information, so a coefficient's conditional interpretation and fitted value can change when another feature is included.
